line.text: The building goes dark mid-click. Her laptop screen drops to a dim nine percent.
Power's out. Nine percent. That's a countdown, not a battery.
Save it. We can just sit.
Already saved. Autosave every two minutes. I'm not an amateur.
She closes the laptop and sets it on the floor. Then she moves to the couch anyway.
No power means no build. No build means nothing to do. Statistically, this is the worst night of the week.

choice.prompt: The dark makes it easy to say something. What do you do?

options.text: You don't have to fill the quiet. I'm not going anywhere.

reaction.text: Her tail, which had gone still, gives one slow curl at the tip.

options.text: You've been running builds all week. When did you last eat?

reaction.text: Her ears flatten for half a second before she catches them.
I'm fine. The build's fine. Everything's handled.

options.text: I noticed you set the kettle on before the lights went out. Thanks.

reaction.text: It was for me. It wasn't for you. Don't make it a thing.
She pushes her fringe back and does not look at you for a while.

options.text: So what's actually wrong with the build? Talk me through it.

reaction.text: It's not wrong. It's unfinished. Those are different things.
She pulls her knees up and stares at the dark screen on the floor.

desc: A power cut: the building goes dark and quiet, her laptop is at nine percent, and there is nothing to do but sit on the couch and talk.
